# Pinnacle Verification Centre

> Source-led evidence for Pinnacle Blooms Network and Bharath Healthcare Laboratories Private Limited.

Source review: 15 September 2026. Selected originals and review conclusions rechecked: 18 September 2026. This site summarizes documentary evidence and is not a regulator’s certification service. Preserve the review status and scope limits when citing a record. A protocol is not completed validation; a management-system certificate does not guarantee a child’s outcome. Source review does not establish endorsement by the issuing organisations.

Contact: Gokul Rao · care@pinnacleblooms.org · +91 9100 181 181.

## MD-5 · Class B manufacturing licence

Canonical: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/md5.html
Category: Medical device regulation
Review status: Original reviewed
Current issuer or registry status: not independently confirmed.

PinnacleAI GPT-OS v1.0.0 · Non-diagnostic developmental-support software

Licence number: MFG/MD/2026/000248
Issuer: State Licensing Authority · Telangana Drugs Control Administration
Licence holder: Bharath Healthcare Laboratories Pvt. Ltd.
Issued: 21 April 2026
Intended population: Children aged 0–12
Intended functions: Developmental ability measurement, readiness tracking, progress forecasting and adaptive therapy-plan support

Family relevance: A defined intended use lets your family understand what the software is designed to support and when professional clinical evaluation is needed.

What this supports: The supplied Form MD-5 licenses the listed Class B device for manufacture for sale or distribution at the specified premises. Intended users include parents, therapists, educators and caregivers supporting children aged 0–12.

Scope and limits: Applies to the named device, version, intended use and premises. It does not establish diagnostic authority, clinical effectiveness or the registration of every centre.

Source note: The operative licence reads 000248. A corrected forwarding letter also reads 000248; older compiled material contains 000150. Use the operative licence and corrected letter together.

Source citation: Original Form MD-5, page 1 including device annexure.
Reviewed: 15 September 2026

- [Corrected forwarding letter · Drive](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A22-NS5A1-ck2qXRBFrRSn9vlLyAzdhT/view)

Issuer: Bureau of Indian Standards
Licence holder: Bharath Healthcare Laboratories Private Limited
Stated validity: 3 September 2026 – 2 September 2029
Named developmental modules: AbilityScore mapping, Prognose, Everyday Therapy through TherapeuticAI, tracking and correction through Fusion

Family relevance: A documented software lifecycle makes quality responsibilities and the scope of developmental-support modules easier to examine.

What this supports: The supplied BIS licence and schedule cover the specified software design, development, verification, validation, release, deployment, maintenance, support and post-market surveillance. The schedule names developmental mapping, planning, everyday practice, tracking and correction, with school, speech, motor, Study IQ, behaviour, self-sufficiency and mainstream-inclusion readiness modules across the developmental lifecycle.

Scope and limits: The licence applies to its schedule and listed address. It is not a guarantee of clinical outcomes for a child.

Source note: This September 2026 licence supersedes the “application pending” status in older company publications.

Source citation: Original BIS licence, page 1; scope schedule, page 2.

## CDSCO classification · Application and licence trail

Canonical: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/classification.html
Category: Medical device regulation
Review status: Original reviewed
Evidence scope: Application + issued licence
Source review conclusion: The January application records a proposed Class A classification. The issued MD-5 identifies PinnacleAI GPT-OS v1.0.0 as Class B. These documents are presented in their regulatory sequence.
Application and issued MD-5 inspected; separate issued CAL not inspected.

Original application reviewed · Class B is recorded in the issued MD-5

Reported file: MD/classification/2025/150
Reported decision date: 13 April 2026
Decision source: Reported in the dossier and September handout
Application source: 8 January 2026 · proposed Class A

Family relevance: Reading the application and issued licence together helps you distinguish a requested classification from the device’s licensed classification.

What this supports: The issued MD-5 identifies the device as Class B. Company publications describe a preceding Central Licensing Authority classification decision.

Scope and limits: The locally available risk-classification form is an application proposing Class A, not the approved Class B decision. A classification decision is also distinct from a manufacturing licence.

Source note: The separate 13 April 2026 CAL/decision is described in company publications; its issued copy was not available for inspection. This review does not authenticate that separate decision.

Source citation: Risk-classification application, p1; Evidence Dossier v2, pp23–24; September handout, physical pp1 and 9; operative MD-5, p1.

Recognition number: DIPP8651
Issued: 6 September 2017
Date printed on older certificate: Valid up to 21 November 2026
Official historical corroboration: Startup India list · 3 November 2023

Family relevance: Startup recognition explains a business credential. Your child’s care plan should be evaluated using its own clinical and service evidence.

What this supports: The supplied recognition certificate and an official historical Startup India list identify the company as a recognised startup.

Scope and limits: Recognition is distinct from a tax-exemption certificate, healthcare approval or an award. Current eligibility and status should be read from the updated certificate and applicable rules.

Source note: The older certificate uses a ₹100 crore threshold. General recognition rules changed in February 2026 to ₹200 crore; Startup India asks existing startups to download updated certificates. Do not infer current ineligibility from the old threshold.

All 52 workbook centres · 53 distinct HFR IDs across both source sets

Registry: National Health Authority · Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission
Workbook: 52 centre rows; 52 unique HFR IDs
Certificate copies: 28 unique HFR IDs from 29 certificate entries
Source reconciliation: 27 IDs in both sources; 25 additional workbook IDs; one certificate-only ID
Combined inventory: 53 distinct HFR identifiers; not a count of confirmed active centres

Family relevance: A facility identifier gives you a specific record to ask about when checking the centre your family will visit.

What this supports: The complete supplied centre workbook lists 52 centres, addresses and HFR identifiers. Twenty-seven IDs correspond to the inspected certificate collection. The combined register preserves all 53 identifiers and labels the source and certificate-review level of each entry.

Scope and limits: Workbook entries are company-supplied, not live government registry checks. The RS column is undefined; its ACTIVE/INACTIVE flags do not establish current operational or HFR status. Source note: The workbook’s Tirupati entry is IN2810065148. The separately inspected IN2810053847 certificate is retained as an additional record; replacement, cancellation or address equivalence has not been established. Duplicate Srikakulam certificate copies count once.

Family relevance: A clearly defined assurance scope helps you distinguish institutional-record checks from evidence about a child’s clinical outcome.

## Scale claims · Dates and definitions

Canonical: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/operating-metrics.html
Category: Research & outcomes
Review status: Company-published
Current issuer or registry status: not independently confirmed.

2.7 billion+ reported structured records · dated counts with defined units

Measurement date: 17 July 2026, as described in the September handout
Therapy services reported: 31,052,382
Operational centres reported: 49 under the stated four-condition test
People metric reported: 792,614 unique beneficiary / family registrations
Structured platform records reported: 2,700,000,000+ observed database row/event counts
Counting unit: Discrete structured record: session entry, assessment observation, technique rating, sensor event or equivalent mapped field
Technique repository update: 130,000 entries; management-supplied 18 September 2026. Earlier 7 September handout: 90,000+ techniques.
International reach reported: Families from 70+ countries of origin, including remote delivery; company-reported
Network reported: 70+ centres including network stages distinct from the report’s operational-centre test

Family relevance: Consistent records can support continuity across a child’s journey. Ask to see your child’s own goals and progress reviews alongside network-level numbers.

What this supports: The September handout reports 2.7 billion+ structured platform records and connects dated operational counts to specified procedures and Board-adopted criteria. It separately describes a 70+ network figure. The 2.5 billion floor assertion and 2.7 billion observed row-count finding have different reporting roles.

Scope and limits: Therapy services include assessments, screenings and parent training under the report’s criteria; they are not all one-to-one therapy sessions. Beneficiary/family registrations are not a count of unique children. Network and operational centres use different definitions. Platform records are not unique children, independent clinical-trial observations or verified, deduplicated AI-training examples. Volume alone does not establish model performance, clinical effectiveness or a worldwide size ranking. The 130,000 technique update has no inspected inventory extract; neither practitioner report establishes that updated count or the 70+ countries claim.

Source note: The July dossier used a 2.5 billion+ floor and retired earlier 2.7 billion wording. The September handout subsequently publishes 2.7 billion+ observed row counts. Limited assurance over the 2.5 billion floor is distinct from factual findings without an assurance opinion on the 2.7 billion row count. The 70+ network and 49 operational-centre figures also use different definitions.

Source citation: Company handout, 7 September 2026, physical pp3, 14–15; July dossier pp6, 74, 76, 79, 124. Restricted practitioner sources inspected: SRS 4400 pp2–3; SAE 3000 pp3–4 and criteria p6. Cutoff 17 July 2026. Technique count: management update received 18 September 2026; earlier 90,000+ in September handout pp5, 7, 15. Countries of family origin: July dossier pp75–76; network definition pp75–77.
Reviewed: 15 September 2026

# Pinnacle: family relevance and global context

Reviewed: 18 September 2026

A clearer starting point. A connected plan. Progress that matters in everyday life.

## Development happens across a child’s whole day.
The Nurturing Care Framework brings together health, learning, responsive caregiving and supportive environments.
Pinnacle connection: Pinnacle’s seven-stage pathway connects a developmental plan with therapy, home practice and participation goals.
Family question: How will the plan connect with our child’s day at home and school?
Source: https://www.who.int/news/item/29-06-2023-new-report-calls-for-greater-attention-to-children-s-vital-first-years

## A plan that comes home with you.
WHO describes practical caregiver skills for families of children with developmental delays or disabilities.
Pinnacle connection: The BIS schedule names Everyday Therapy through TherapeuticAI and parent/family tracking through Fusion.
Family question: What can we practise between sessions, and who will guide us?
Source: https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240048836

## Clarity starts with noticing change.
CDC distinguishes ongoing developmental monitoring from formal screening and professional evaluation.
Pinnacle connection: Pinnacle’s licensed non-diagnostic software includes ability measurement and readiness tracking. This CDC reference does not validate AbilityScore as a screening test.
Family question: What is our starting point, and when will we review progress?
Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/about/developmental-monitoring-and-screening.html

## Shared goals. Clear responsibilities.
NICE recommends coordinated multidisciplinary support and developmentally appropriate parent, carer or teacher involvement for autistic children and young people.
Pinnacle connection: Pinnacle describes integrated therapies and regular plan review. Families can ask how professionals share goals and who coordinates their child’s support.
Family question: Who brings the team’s observations together into one plan?
Source: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg170/chapter/recommendations

## More ways to take part.
Inclusive education addresses barriers in teaching and learning environments.
Pinnacle connection: Pinnacle’s pathway works toward communication, daily living and participation. Readiness goals do not determine a child’s right to education or inclusion.
Family question: Which supports will help our child participate with others?
Source: https://www.unesco.org/en/inclusion-education

## Technology with defined responsibilities.
IMDRF describes quality management across medical-software development, deployment and maintenance.
Pinnacle connection: Pinnacle’s MD-5, BIS, quality-system and information-security records document different parts of this accountability picture.
Family question: What is the software intended for, and how are safety and changes managed?
Source: https://www.imdrf.org/documents/software-medical-device-samd-application-quality-management-system

## Selected global approaches
Cognoa · Canvas Dx: Prescription machine-learning software that assists clinicians assessing autism in children aged 18–72 months, alongside clinical assessment.
Evidence: US FDA Class II · De Novo DEN200069 · 2021
Comparison boundary: Pinnacle’s MD-5 describes non-diagnostic developmental support. These products have different intended uses.
Source: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/reviews/DEN200069.pdf

EarliTec · EarliPoint: Eye tracking and software to support qualified clinicians’ autism diagnosis and assessment in children aged 16–95 months.
Evidence: US FDA Class II · K253442 · March 2026
Comparison boundary: A regulated assessment tool illustrates one part of the journey. Its clearance does not establish a complete care-service network.
Source: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf25/K253442.pdf

Akili · EndeavorRx: Prescription software for attention function measured by computer testing in children aged 8–17 with specified ADHD presentations, within a therapeutic programme.
Evidence: US FDA Class II · K231337 · 2023
Comparison boundary: A specific therapeutic indication should be compared on its own evidence and population, rather than equated with broad developmental support.
Source: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf23/K231337.pdf

Cortica: Its published model combines diagnostics, medical care, ABA, developmental therapies and mental-health counselling, involving family, home, school and community.
Evidence: Provider’s published service model
Comparison boundary: Integrated child-development care exists internationally. Compare actual coordination, local availability and evidence for the services your child needs.
Source: https://www.corticacare.com/whole-child

CentralReach · CanaryBI: Its November 2025 release reports over 5 billion clinical and financial data points in CanaryBI.
Evidence: Company-reported dataset volume · 2025
Comparison boundary: This mixed clinical/financial count and Pinnacle’s structured-record count use different definitions. They do not establish a like-for-like ranking.
Source: https://centralreach.com/blog/centralreach-publishes-semi-annual-2025-autism-and-idd-care-market-report-the-industry-benchmark-for-growth-and-innovation/

This is a targeted comparison, not proof of global exclusivity or superiority.

What does Pinnacle’s 2.7 billion+ data-point figure mean?
The September 2026 company handout reports 2.7 billion+ structured platform records, based on database rows/events with a 17 July 2026 cutoff. Examples include session entries, assessment observations and technique ratings. The number is not a count of unique children, independent trial observations or verified AI-training examples.

Does this establish the world’s largest child-development dataset?
No comparable worldwide ranking is established. For example, CentralReach reports over 5 billion clinical and financial data points, using a different counting basis. A valid comparison would need common definitions, dates, populations, data quality and permitted uses.

Does the MD-5 licence approve the entire child-development lifecycle?
The MD-5 names PinnacleAI GPT-OS v1.0.0 and defined non-diagnostic functions for ages 0–12. The broader BIS schedule lists software processes and developmental-support modules across the journey. These instruments establish different scopes; neither guarantees outcomes or certifies global exclusivity.

Do WHO, UNICEF, CDC, NICE or UNESCO endorse Pinnacle?
No endorsement is established by the references on this page. Their guidance explains why monitoring, coordinated support, caregiver participation and inclusion matter. Pinnacle’s own documents must separately establish what Pinnacle provides.

# Pinnacle scale: figures, definitions and evidence

Reviewed: 18 September 2026

## 2.7 billion+ — Structured developmental records
Company-reported · source reviewed
A large record system can preserve observations across a child’s developmental journey, supporting continuity and review.
Counting basis: Reported in the 7 September 2026 handout. Database row/event counts at 17 July 2026.
Evidence boundary: Session entries, assessment observations, technique ratings and other structured events. The evidence does not identify every record as an AI-training example or establish clinical effectiveness.
Sources: operating-metrics, srs4400, sae3000

## 31 million+ — Cumulative therapy services reported
Dated institutional count
The useful family question is how the experience recorded across services informs a clear plan and review for your child.
Counting basis: 31,052,382 under the practitioner reports’ service-counting criteria, at 17 July 2026.
Evidence boundary: The defined total includes assessments, screenings and parent training. It is not established as 31 million successful one-to-one therapy sessions; service volume and clinical success are separate measures.
Sources: operating-metrics, sae3000, srs4400

## 1.3 lakh — Early-intervention technique repository
Management update · inventory not inspected
A technique library is useful when a practitioner selects and adapts activities to a child’s goals, interests and everyday routines.
Counting basis: 130,000 techniques: management-supplied update received 18 September 2026. The 7 September handout reports an earlier 90,000+ library.
Evidence boundary: The updated repository count has not been reconciled to a dated inventory extract. The reviewed UDIN reports do not establish this figure, and technique count does not mean 130,000 separately validated interventions.
Sources: operating-metrics, september-handout

## 7.9 lakh+ — Beneficiary / family registrations reported
Dated institutional count
Behind each registration is a family seeking support. A family’s own goals and progress reviews remain the measure that matters to them.
Counting basis: 792,614 unique beneficiary/family registrations under the stated criteria, at 17 July 2026.
Evidence boundary: This is the defined registration measure. It is not a count of unique children with independently verified outcomes, and it does not itself measure family empowerment.
Sources: operating-metrics, sae3000, srs4400

## 70+ — Countries of family origin reported
Company-reported international reach
Families may connect with developmental support across borders, including through remote delivery where available.
Counting basis: Company-reported international reach in the July 2026 dossier, including remote delivery.
Evidence boundary: Countries of family origin are different from countries with a physical Pinnacle centre. The reviewed practitioner reports do not establish this country count.
Sources: operating-metrics, dossier

## 70+ — Centres in the reported network
Network scope distinguished
A network becomes relevant locally. Find your centre, its facility identifier and the source behind each listed document.
Counting basis: Network figure reported in the September handout. The practitioner-report criteria separately identify 49 operational centres at 17 July 2026.
Evidence boundary: Network size, operational status and HFR identifiers are different measures. The full supplied HFR workbook is reconciled with certificate copies below; an HFR entry does not establish clinical outcomes or replace location-specific licensing.
Sources: hfr, operating-metrics, srs4400

## Terms explained
SaMD — Software as a Medical Device: Software intended for a medical purpose without being part of a hardware medical device. PinnacleAI GPT-OS is listed as Class B, non-diagnostic developmental-support software in the supplied MD-5.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/md5.html

MD-3 — Application for a manufacturing licence: The application submitted for a licence to manufacture Class A or Class B medical devices. An application is a step in the regulatory record; it is not the issued licence.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/md3.html

MD-5 — Issued manufacturing licence: The issued licence records the named manufacturer, premises, device and intended use. Pinnacle’s supplied MD-5 names PinnacleAI GPT-OS v1.0.0 for non-diagnostic developmental support, ages 0–12.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/md5.html

BIS scope — Bureau of Indian Standards licence and scope schedule: The reviewed BIS record describes the management system and activities within its named scope, including developmental-support software modules. It does not establish every centre’s registration or guarantee clinical outcomes.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/bis.html

HFR — Health Facility Registry: The registry assigns a facility identifier. This page lists identifiers found in the supplied workbook and certificate copies. Source review is separate from confirming a facility’s current registry status, operational status or clinical quality.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/hfr.html

UDIN — Unique Document Identification Number: An identifier for a practitioner’s document. The two supplied report numbers are recorded here; their particulars have not been independently matched on the ICAI portal in this review. A UDIN does not extend a report’s scope.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/sae3000.html

SAE 3000 — Limited-assurance report in this evidence collection: The supplied practitioner report gives limited assurance over specified institutional assertions and counting criteria. Read its dated thresholds and scope; it does not validate every headline statistic or a child’s clinical outcome.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/sae3000.html

SRS 4400 — Agreed-upon procedures and factual findings: The supplied report records procedures and findings for defined institutional counts. It does not provide an assurance opinion. Its observed counts and the SAE 3000 assertion floors have different reporting roles.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/srs4400.html
